success_patterns: Every success had the clue's distinctive words repeated almost verbatim across many passages, either in an archive line ('... | Punxsutawney Phil.') or in several titles and snippets (Luther Burbank, Tootsie, Anastasia, Smithsonian Institution). The agent took the entity that recurs next to the clue's details, and gave it in the short form the passages use.

The agent matched the category noun after 'this' (city, empire, institution, position, film, horticulturist) and answered an instance of that category, never a word from the clue. Marius and Cinna 'captured this city' gave Rome. 'This position' gave 'center'.
Quoted-word puns were resolved by finding the passage where the quoted word sits beside a candidate. 'Drag' sat beside Dustin Hoffman and Tootsie, and 'Tootsie' was the answer.
Head nouns were kept only where the passages use them as part of the standard name ('Roman Empire', 'Smithsonian Institution'). Plain generic nouns were left lowercase and bare ('center').
All eight answers were one-step: no overthinking, no added descriptors, and no override of the well-supported entity.

patch.reasoning: All eight successes were handled by rules already in the skill: Rule 3 (verbatim or repeated-passage match), Rule 2 (category-noun referent and quoted-word hints), and Rule 4 (bare answer, head-noun exception). Eleven recent patch attempts were rejected, each lowering the score by adding more rules to an already long skill. Adding another rule would likely cause the same regression, and nothing observed here is uncovered, so I propose no edits.
